description.p: Chassis is a graphical device manager for Linux that lets you browse, inspect, and manage your hardware. View detailed information about all system devices, including GPUs, storage drives, sensors, and network adapters.

ul.li: Browse devices by category: Graphics, Networking, Storage, Audio, USB, and more
Live sensor readings with temperature, fan speed, voltage, and power monitoring
GPU details including VRAM, clocks, PCIe link, and display outputs
Display and monitor info from EDID: model, resolution, refresh rate, and physical size
Storage drive health with SMART data and NVMe temperature tracking
Network interface details including link speed, state, and wireless/Bluetooth detection
CPU, memory module, and motherboard information
Camera, serial port, and USB debug probe detection
Security key, RGB controller, and portable device recognition
Bluetooth device detection with battery monitoring
Kernel driver management (bind, unbind, change drivers)
Live hotplug: devices appear and disappear as you plug them in
Hardware resource details: IRQ assignments, memory regions, and I/O ports
Adaptive layout for any screen size

description.p: Most features work without elevated privileges. A system daemon provides additional capabilities including driver management, SMART data, and SMBIOS information.
Initial release with comprehensive hardware detection and monitoring.
